title: C212 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
I use this reference as a seating chart for the wiring: the drawing locates a cavity, and the matching table row tells you what belongs there. Start with the connector identification, then check the face and harness heading before using its circuit table. Similar-looking housings are a poor substitute for matching identifiers.

In the drawing as displayed, a vertical column sits at the far right, paired columns run through the center, and another column sits at the far left. Read the printed cavity labels rather than counting across the gaps. Use Cavity to move from drawing to table, then read Circuit Number, Color and Function together. This connector brings together fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies, control signals and network connections; sharing a housing does not give those wires the same job.

This is an identification and circuit-reading reference. It does not establish physical access, the viewing direction on the vehicle, release movements or an electrical test. The Gauge convention and the Size and Used codes are not explained here, so retain those entries literally rather than turning them into wire-selection advice. Once you have identified a circuit, its diagnostic or service procedure supplies the next action.

Read the male and female tables separately. The female table records unqualified transmission-signal-return and speed-control-command-return alternatives at the same cavity. Their matching color and terminal fields do not select an applicable function or establish that the circuits are joined. Populated male entries also face blank female entries in the source, so matching cavity labels alone do not establish a complete physical wiring configuration.

edits.why: The face and harness labels identify which drawing and accompanying hardware record belong together. I use the housing outline and rectangular features as visual landmarks only; their appearance does not establish a latch or release function. The MALE label alone does not establish the physical viewing direction.

Each row connects a cavity label to its recorded circuit details and terminal part number. Gray-filled positions are a cue to consult the corresponding row, not evidence of an electrical fault. Keep Function and Qualifier together, including any protection alternatives and polarity labels. A relay is an electrically controlled switch, but its name does not guarantee a separate plug-in component. A LIN bus carries messages rather than serving as a simple on/off power wire; the function label therefore matters as much as the wire's appearance.

I use this heading to keep the female drawing with its own harness and parts table. As drawn, cavity columns sit along the left edge, through the paired center area and along the right edge, with horizontal housing features interrupting the center. Those shapes are landmarks, not identified release controls. The physical viewing direction is unspecified.

Treat the drawing as an address book: find the cavity label, then read its complete circuit row. Shaded cavities with supplied rows correspond to blank circuit entries, but shading is no diagnosis. Distinguish fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies, relay functions, commands and communication lines; a relay label does not guarantee a separate plug-in part, and LIN carries messages. Preserve repeated entries without choosing an unstated configuration. Gauge convention and Size/Used code definitions remain outside this reference, which supplies no access, probing or test procedure.

originalAuthorHold: Female cavity 30 has unqualified entries for RE406 transmission signal return and RES08 speed-control command return. Both are retained; their shared color and terminal information do not establish which function applies.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 108 primary units, six complete pages/two figures and four edits. Original first CLI author covered 55 units and the second held author covered 49 units; both authors and the complete first-chunk verdict remain preserved separately. Complete draft includes the remaining source tail and explicitly retains female return-function alternatives and cross-face populated-versus-blank differences. Physical configurations remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
